neighbours.label: the US constitutional order (Congress, the Supreme Court, the President's powers, amendments), as opposed to the same frames for clubs, councils and other countries' institutions
fire: In 1952 the Supreme Court stopped Truman from seizing the steel mills.
Congress shall make no law respecting a religion.
Congress has the power to declare war under the Constitution.
The Fourth Amendment bars unreasonable searches by the government.
The states are prevented from coining their own money.
The President may veto any bill sent by Congress.
The Constitution provides for a census every ten years.
The Court held that the law violates the Equal Protection Clause.
quiet: In 1952 the headmaster stopped the janitor from selling the school desks.
The parish council shall make no rule on Sunday markets.
The board has the power to fire staff under the contract.
The club bars unruly guests from the dining room.
The tenants are prevented from keeping their own dogs.
The Queen may dissolve the Parliament at the request of the Prime Minister.
Every fruit tree shall bear its seed and be food for you.
The German court held that the law violates the Basic Law.

notes: Card: ' the', ' to', ' shall', ' The', ' of', ' or', scattered, with Congress, Supreme Court and the Constitution among them. Probes: 'ordered Nixon to' 0.63, 'provides for ... general' 0.42, 'Senate ... power to' 0.41, 'Court ruled ... must' 0.37, 'prevented from' 0.25, 'First Amendment' 0.21; club, parish and referee versions, Parliament and Bundestag 0.03 or less. Weaker: 'Every law must be passed by both houses' 0.12. Newton's law reached 0.30 and 0.10, and biblical 'shall be' is on the card, so 'binding rules' more widely is a rival, tested here by one biblical near miss.
